headline: Brands are starting to rewrite their marketing for AI shopping agents instead of human shoppers.
score_reason: Trend feature with solid numbers, but no single new event; kept at the pool score.
importance_line: Shoppers may soon see products chosen by an agent's logic rather than by ads, small retailers face new fees to stay visible to those agents, and analysts warn the tactics may age quickly as the models change.
summary: The New York Times reports, as carried by The Business Times, that a new crop of startups such as Limy, New Generation and Gauge is helping brands rework their websites and product data so that AI shopping agents from Meta and OpenAI will pick their goods, with one cabinetry retailer already paying $15,000 for the makeover. Adobe says AI-driven traffic to US retail sites rose 393 percent this year and Morgan Stanley estimates agent-influenced spending could reach about $385 billion by 2030, though some marketers caution that the models shift too fast for any trick to last.
notes: NYT original blocked; text read on The Business Times (Singapore), which credits NYTIMES.
